title: Registry isolation missed browser APIs that parse and materialize untrusted HTML

examples: bound, destructured, and reflected forms of the same sinks
reproduction.beforeFix: The gate returned pass for contextual-fragment parsing, DOMParser parsing, and setHTMLUnsafe, including bound/destructured/reflected aliases.
reproduction.afterFix: The gate rejects these unsafe HTML materialization sinks while retaining the safe setHTML API path covered by a positive regression.

rootCause: The scanner checked common React and DOM raw-HTML setters but did not classify newer or indirect browser parsing APIs that turn strings into DOM nodes.
remediation: Track and reject createContextualFragment, DOMParser.parseFromString, and setHTMLUnsafe through aliases, destructuring, binding, and reflection as unsafe markup sinks; retain the explicitly tested safe setHTML case.

validation.redBeforeFix: pnpm exec vitest run packages/registry-gate/src/__tests__/registry-gate.test.ts -t "browser HTML parsing sinks"
validation.redBeforeFixResult: failed as expected: all covered parsing sinks were admitted before the fix

runtimeBoundary: This is static registry source analysis. The probes were parsed only and never executed. The separate preview CSP and origin sandbox remain required defenses; deployment verification remains pending.
